clarity_findings.claim: The 'While besieged' bullet crams six blocked actions into one list item, which slows the reader down.
clarity_findings.problem: "No one can order buildings, repairs or ships, cancel orders, destroy buildings, or place or recall agents." strings together three different verb groups (order X/Y/Z, cancel orders, destroy buildings, place or recall agents) with repeated 'or's. It's grammatically fine and under the 25-word cap, so it isn't a lint violation, but a reader has to parse five separate blocked actions out of one run-on clause, and "cancel orders" briefly reads like it could mean something else before the next clause disambiguates it.
clarity_findings.fix: Split into two bullets, e.g. "No one can order buildings, repairs or ships." and "No one can cancel an order, destroy a building, or place or recall agents." (matches the list style already used elsewhere in the manual, e.g. the buildings guide brief).

clarity_findings.claim: The closing sentence of the Pillage yield section is harder to parse than it needs to be.
clarity_findings.problem: "A pillage's loot uses the yield the system had before that same pillage lowers it." packs two references to "it"/"that same pillage" back to back, forcing a re-read to confirm which pillage and which yield value is meant.
clarity_findings.fix: Reword for a single clear referent, e.g. "The loot is calculated from the yield the system had before this pillage lowers it."

votes.reason: Siege's effects and damage rules read clean in one pass, but the Pillage yield section needs a second read to sort out its stacked exceptions and vague magnitude.
stumbles: "takes a multiple of the system's credit, technology and ideology output from its owner's stock" never says what the multiple actually is (a fixed number of hours of output? unstated), so "55% of what it would take at 100" is a percentage of an unknown base amount.

"A Navarch who is killed or forced to flee a fight before the attack resolves also lowers it by 15" sits right after the "when an attack resolves" sentence, so it reads at first like a third resolve-outcome before you notice it's actually describing a fight that never resolves.
"A pillage's loot uses the yield the system had before that same pillage lowers it" is a dense, self-referential ordering clarification ('that same pillage') that takes a re-read to parse.

votes.reason: Rules are stated directly with one concrete worked example (55 yield → 55%), but two phrases needed a second pass to parse.
stumbles: "depending on its result" (in "can kill population and damage buildings, depending on its result") doesn't say what determines the result, so it reads as a dangling reference on first pass

"A pillage's loot uses the yield the system had before that same pillage lowers it" — the self-referential "that same pillage" phrasing took a re-read to confirm it means pre-attack yield, not post-attack
the building table's "twice as likely to be picked as the others" has no baseline stated (twice as likely as what number/chance), so it's clear only in relative terms
